newsitem.title: USA: Cash flow to long-term funds $19.5 bln in August.
newsitem.headline: Cash flow to long-term funds $19.5 bln in August.

text.p: A surge in new money put into stock funds fueled a big rise in fresh investments going into long-term funds in August, the Investment Company Institute said Wednesday.
Net new cash flow to stock, bond and income mutual funds reached $19.5 billion in August, compared with $4.8 billion in July, ICI, the trade group representing the mutual fund industry, said.
New investments in stock funds were estimated at $19.0 billion in August, up sharply from $5.8 billion of net flows in July, ICI said.

"The resumption of strong inflows to stock funds came amid a backdrop of generally rising stock prices and reduced price volatility," in sharp contrast to the market developments in July, said ICI chief economist John Rea.
But while August's estimate for stock funds is historically high, Rea said it is well off the $24.7 billion monthly average of new cash flow posted over the first five months of 1996.
The $500 million net flows registered among bond and income funds compared with an outflow of $1.04 billion in July, ICI said.
The inflow reversed two back-to-back months of small outflows and appeared to be a continuation of sluggish flows to those funds that began in February, Rea said.
